title: DeciderSettings
description: Data file content/decider/settings.json: when inhabitants ask the decider (W1595: whatever an inhabitant does not understand becomes a question to the AI; B2487: questions wait without a fixed time limit), and the environment values used until weather (B2) and temperature (B5) exist. Placeholders until Marcel decides.

deadline_ms.description: Service time budget per request (ADR-0006); the core itself never waits for the clock.

max_open_questions.description: Open questions per inhabitant at the same time, whether with the decider or waiting (held back, or for the night). A question of a trigger that interrupts is not kept out by questions that only wait.

retry_after_minutes.description: After a retryable ServiceError the question stays open and is sent again after this many game minutes (B2487: no fixed time limit).

ask_cooldown_hours.description: Game hours before the same inhabitant asks about the same subject again.

choice_protection_hours.description: One thing at a time (A1487): while a question of an inhabitant is with the decider, or a choice the decider made for it is queued or under way (walking there or doing it), no further question of that inhabitant goes to the decider - it opens with its question mark and is asked once the inhabitant is free again, if what raised it still holds (the thing or the other still in sight and not understood); otherwise it lapses (question_failed, detail lapsed) and the trigger raises it anew when it sees the thing again. This value is the time limit in game hours: it bounds what has no end of its own - a question that is out with the decider, the walk to a chosen target, a choice queued behind a walk; older than this they no longer hold anything back. An action that runs ends by its duration, and with it the wait of a choice queued behind it, so these need no limit. Exceptions: triggers with interrupts, and a choice that serves none of the needs below their neglect_below (inhabitant model). Omitted or 0 = questions are never held back (as before).

max_requests_per_step.description: At most this many requests go to the decider in one step (tick), whatever raised them: new questions, questions that waited (held back) and questions sent again after an error or after loading a save. What is over waits with its question mark and goes out in the next steps, in the order it would have gone. Bounds the one step in which many questions fall due together - all held-back questions at the end of choice_protection_hours, every open question after loading a save. Omitted = no limit (as before).

unknown_inhabitant_max_asks.description: How often an inhabitant asks who the same other inhabitant is (trigger unknown_inhabitant) while it never learns the name; omitted = no limit.

Trigger.description: A kind of not-understanding that becomes a question.

kind.description: unknown_object: a thing of a type without any belief in sight; noticed_player: the player noticed (click); unknown_inhabitant: another inhabitant in sight whose own name it does not know (B4a R8).

ask.description: When the question goes to the AI (A1487): immediate = to the decider the moment it opens (as before); night = it opens with its question mark, is not sent to the decider by day and is answered by the compute night's question job (knowledge settings: night_questions must list the trigger; only for questions about an object type). Omitted = immediate. A later value will follow the day's contingent (D713).

interrupts.description: Whether a question of this trigger goes to the decider even while its inhabitant is busy with another question or an accepted choice (choice_protection_hours); its answer then replaces that choice, as before. Omitted = false: the question waits.
